answer: Each identity books one pearl dive at a ridge cove and locks a 70-credit bond to its dive key. At horizon dawn it must surface within ten minutes and file a signed catch log. An auditor checks the manifest, surfacing time, and log key; a missed window, mismatched key, or shared boat burns the bond. The first dive costs 38 credits; the kth fake costs 38+6(k-1), so the 1000th costs 6032 and 1000 fakes cost 3,035,000 plus 70,000 locked. A rented-diver ring fails because one diver cannot surface at two ridge coves in one horizon window. An honest diver pays 38 once and recovers the bond if clean.
